learnings: Secondary token changed from dark (black bg/white text) to light (96% lightness bg/dark text) — button.tsx spinner uses stroke-background for secondary variant which will be invisible. Fix in future iteration.
data-table-select-popover.tsx uses bg-secondary for checkbox selected state — will be invisible with light secondary. Needs bg-primary text-primary-foreground instead.
Differentiate --accent (93%) from --muted (96%) by 3 lightness points to preserve hover visibility on muted surfaces.
builder-background-pattern shifted to hsl(220 8% 72%) to align with blue-gray palette instead of pure gray #b2b2b2.
When changing token semantics (dark→light), audit all stroke-* and bg-* usages that depend on the old contrast relationship. Simplify conditionals where possible.

For inline checkboxes in popovers, use border-primary in both selected and unselected states so the control boundary is always visible against white backgrounds. Use opacity-50 for the unselected state to keep it subtle.
FlowSidebarItem was not passing isActive to SidebarMenuButton, so CVA data-active styles (font-medium) never fired. Always check that component props are wired through, not just className overrides.
SidebarMenuButton CVA default size is h-8. Any py-* override expands beyond 32px, breaking vertical rhythm. Use CVA size variants instead of manual padding.

Unify active-state pattern across all sidebar item types: bg-sidebar-primary/10 text-sidebar-primary. Avoid bg-sidebar-accent for active states — it reads as hover, not selection. Also avoid !important overrides when cn() ordering suffices.

Content cards that sit on bg-sidebar background already have 3 separation signals: color contrast, border, shadow. The shadow is redundant — remove it and rely on border per design spec. Don't replace with shadow-sm either.
Builder-layout uses p-1.5 (6px) while project-layout uses p-2 pt-3 pb-3 (8px/12px). Future iteration should unify wrapper padding across sibling layouts.

Table column headers should use text-muted-foreground font-normal to be visually subordinate to data rows. Align all three hierarchy signals (size, weight, color) in the same direction — don't use font-medium to compensate for muted color.

For structural/container icons (folders), use text-muted-foreground/70 — subordinate to semantic icons (text-primary for flows, text-emerald-500 for tables) but clearly from the design token system. Never use raw Tailwind grays (gray-400) which have hue 0° instead of the 220° cool blue-gray palette.

DataTableColumnHeader -ml-3 on sortable button is a negative margin violation but compensates for table cell padding. Audit th/td padding before removing — otherwise sortable headers will appear indented.
Sort icon active state: use text-foreground when sortDirection is truthy, text-muted-foreground when unsorted. Resolved in iteration #23.
Vite build has pre-existing zod resolution failure — use tsc --noEmit for verification when vite build is broken.

For table cell links (navigable counts, IDs), use text-primary hover:underline cursor-pointer transition-colors duration-150 wrapped in cn(). Don't use permanent underline — reveal on hover matches Linear/Retool table cell link pattern. Don't use hover:text-primary-300 as it's darker, not lighter.

For inline separators between metadata items, use <div className="h-4 w-px bg-border" /> — the established codebase pattern. Never use bare text pipe characters. The parent gap utility handles spacing automatically.
font-sm is not a valid Tailwind class — always use font-normal (400), font-medium (500), or font-semibold (600). Tailwind font-* classes are for weight, not size (use text-sm for size).

Any sidebar-like nav panel in dialogs (settings, etc.) must use the same active-state pattern as the main sidebar: bg-sidebar-primary/10 hover:bg-sidebar-primary/15 text-sidebar-primary. Include hover override on active items to prevent hover:bg-sidebar-accent from overriding the primary tint.

Dialog/panel headings must use font-semibold tracking-tight (matching DialogTitle primitive), never font-bold. The DialogTitle in dialog.tsx line 128 is the canonical text-lg heading style — all equivalent headings should match it.
CenteredPage is used by 10 platform admin pages — fixing shared layout components propagates design consistency more efficiently than fixing individual pages.

For inline text links in content areas, use text-primary font-medium hover:underline underline-offset-4 transition-colors duration-150. Always remove dark: prefixed overrides — this is a light-mode-only redesign. Never use hardcoded Tailwind colors (text-blue-600) for links when a design token exists.

For status icon/color default cases, use text-muted-foreground — the design system token for secondary/indeterminate content. Don't use two different gray levels (gray-500 vs gray-600) for icon and text of the same semantic state.

When Input/component already has token-based styling via its base class (inputClass), don't override with hardcoded colors in the consumer. Strip all color/border/padding overrides and keep only layout constraints (max-w, flex). The base component is the single source of truth for visual styling.

Button default variant already renders bg-primary text-primary-foreground hover:bg-primary/90 — never override with hardcoded color classes. Remove the className entirely rather than replacing with bg-primary, to avoid tailwind-merge conflicts.

For standalone page cards (login, auth), use shadow-sm instead of drop-shadow-xl. drop-shadow-* uses CSS filter (alpha-shape shadow) while shadow-* uses box-shadow (rectangular). shadow-sm is semantically correct for card elevation and matches shadcn/ui Card conventions. Layout cards inside sidebar containers should use no shadow at all (border only).

Button variant hover classes must use enabled:hover: not bare hover: — matches the pattern in default/outline/secondary/accent/basic variants. Bare hover: fires on disabled buttons (especially with asChild/Slot where the host element may not be a native button). Ghost variant uses enabled:hover:bg-accent enabled:hover:text-accent-foreground.

For skeleton/loading placeholders, use bg-border (91% lightness) not bg-muted (96%) — bg-muted is nearly invisible against #FAFAFA background (96% vs 98% = 1.03:1 contrast), especially at the 50% opacity dim phase of animate-pulse. bg-border provides enough contrast (91% vs 98% = 1.18:1) to remain perceptible throughout the animation cycle.

For interactive card hover/selected borders, use border-foreground/20 — darkens subtly within the 220° hue family. Don't use border-primary for multi-select card borders (warm red reads as error/warning). Reserve border-primary for single focused/active items only.

When a component has both hover and selected border states, differentiate with opacity: hover at /20 (subtle affordance), selected at /25 (slightly stronger confirmation). Same token, different weight — perceptible without introducing new colors.

Place transition-colors as a base class, not inside hover: variant — hover:transition-colors only applies the transition on hover entry, so mouse-out snaps back immediately without animation. Base transition-colors governs both enter and exit symmetrically.

For small status indicator dots (w-2 h-2) in disabled/off state, use bg-border — it's a neutral surface token at 91% lightness, semantically appropriate for inactive indicators. Don't use bg-muted-foreground (a text/icon token, not a surface token). bg-border is already used on the outline badge's own border, making the visual relationship coherent.

For composite input containers (tag-input, multi-select), mirror the canonical inputClass tokens: border-input, bg-background, has-focus-visible:ring-ring, placeholder:text-muted-foreground. Don't use hardcoded neutral-* or bg-white — they bypass the 220° cool blue-gray token system and will look hue-mismatched next to standard Input components in composed forms.

For SVG stroke elements using stroke='currentColor', apply color via text-{token} class — same token routing as HTML elements but rendered as a stroke. text-border works for passive/track circles, text-foreground for bold data text, text-muted-foreground for subordinate labels.

Ghost commit pattern: always run git diff --stat before committing to verify BOTH the source file and tracker files are staged. Iterations #26 and #29 both had tracker-only commits where the actual code change was never staged.

For form field helper/description text, prefer <FormDescription> over bare <div className='text-sm text-muted-foreground'>. FormDescription already includes those classes AND wires aria-describedby via FormItem context, so the field is accessible to screen readers. Place it inside <FormItem> as a sibling to <FormControl>.

Systematic dark: cleanup across shared UI components. Done: badge.tsx (#37), alert.tsx (#38), button.tsx (#39), checkbox.tsx (#40), radio-group.tsx (#41), input.tsx (#42), textarea.tsx (#43), toggle.tsx (#44), select.tsx (#49 — re-fix of ghost commit #45), context-menu.tsx (#46), dropdown-menu.tsx (#47), calendar.tsx (#48), switch.tsx (#50). Remaining: chart.tsx (THEMES constant is structural, not a simple dark: class — needs different approach). Also: switch.tsx shadow-lg on thumb should be downgraded to shadow-sm in next iteration.

For semantic alert/badge text on light backgrounds, use the -700 step (e.g. text-destructive-700, text-warning-700) — high chroma at ~41% lightness clears WCAG AA (4.5:1). Never use -300 (82% lightness, ~1.5:1 contrast) — that's the dark-mode-only tint. Pattern: border-{semantic}/50 text-{semantic}-700 [&>svg]:text-{semantic}.

For small interactive thumb/knob elements (switches, sliders), use shadow-sm not shadow-lg. shadow-lg's 15px blur exceeds the element's own dimensions at small sizes, creating a disproportionate halo. shadow-sm provides enough lift to separate thumb from track without visual noise. Design spec: shadow-lg is reserved for dropdowns/modals only.

For copy/action buttons in code blocks, apply text-muted-foreground on the Button element itself (not the wrapper div) so ghost variant hover/active states can override the muted color during interactions. Wrapper div should only carry positioning classes.

FlowMarkdown Container uses raw Tailwind colors (bg-amber-50, text-amber-700) for WARNING variant instead of semantic tokens (bg-warning-50, text-warning-700). Values are equivalent but should be migrated in a follow-up for full token consistency with alert.tsx base component.

All in-scope dark: overrides now cleaned. Remaining out-of-scope: chart.tsx (structural THEMES constant), flow-canvas files. billing/success.tsx downgrade case uses raw orange-50/600 instead of semantic warning tokens — follow-up for token migration.

When status badge class strings have duplicate conflicting border classes (e.g. border-amber-200 and border-amber-500), keep the -200 step to match sibling variants (success and error both use -200). The duplicate was likely a leftover from an earlier iteration.

Never add shadow overrides to PopoverContent — the base component already supplies shadow-md which is the correct elevation for floating panels. All 15 PopoverContent usages now rely on the base shadow consistently. drop-shadow-xl on popovers was the only remaining in-scope drop-shadow-xl.

All font-bold heading outliers now fixed: accept-invitation (#66), LockedFeatureGuard (#67), view-release (#68), share-template (#69), 404-page (#70). code-editor.tsx uses font-bold for active tab state (builder-chrome) — different pattern, intentional emphasis. Small icon letters (search-result-item, sidebar project avatar, impact pages) use font-bold at text-xs/text-[10px] for decorative purposes — leave alone. share-template.tsx also has border-2 shadow-lg on Card which is heavier than design system spec (border + shadow-sm) — follow-up candidate.
